romanos.descripcion: Julius Caesar, Spartacus, Augustus and Marcus Aurelius with the expired garum and counterfeit currency as punishments. It is the theme of those who watched too many historical series, and also of those who only know Caesar.

preguntas.q: What is garum?
preguntas.a: A fermented fish sauce very popular in Rome; in the game it appears expired as a bad item.

egipto.descripcion: Tutankhamun, Cleopatra, Ramses II and Nefertiti dominate an auction with the sand tray and wet papyrus as counterpoint. The most archaeological theme in the catalog and one of the most beautiful in terms of visual theme.

preguntas.q: Why does a sand tray come out?
preguntas.a: Because today the Egyptian deserts are full of remains of tourists; in the auction it is a bad item with a joke.

samurais.descripcion: Miyamoto Musashi, Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu and Hattori Hanzo against a dented katana and rusty armor. A theme of honor and strategy, where bad items are just the opposite of a good samurai.

preguntas.q: Who was Miyamoto Musashi?
preguntas.a: The most famous samurai and duelist in Japanese history, author of the Book of Five Rings; it is the most valuable item of the theme.

vaqueros.descripcion: Wyatt Earp, Billy the Kid, Doc Holliday and Jesse James at an Old West auction, with broken boots and a broken lasso as punishment. The theme of duels at sundown, perfect for those who grew up on westerns.

preguntas.q: Who is Doc Holliday?
preguntas.a: The dentist and gunslinger who accompanied Wyatt Earp in the O.K. Corral duel; it is one of the most bid-on items.

espacio.descripcion: Apollo 11, the Hubble telescope, Voyager 1 and the Curiosity rover compete with a leaky suit and a floating screw. The most fascinating theme in the catalog, and the one that works best with someone who enjoys explaining space missions.

preguntas.q: What is the most valuable item in space?
preguntas.a: Apollo 11 is usually the most contested, with Hubble and Voyager close behind.

robots.descripcion: R2-D2, WALL-E, Terminator and Optimus Prime in the same auction, with the toy robot and the scrap arm being bad items. A theme that mixes cinema and reality, perfect for science fiction fans.

preguntas.q: Is it a movie theme or a real technology theme?
preguntas.a: Mix: The main items are very recognizable fictional robots, with some nods to real robotics.

animales.descripcion: Wild lion, golden eagle and dolphin compete with the Labrador puppy, the orange kitten and even an axolotl, while the pet cockroach and the buzzing mosquito wait their turn. It is the most tender theme in the catalog, and also the funniest when the bad items show up.

preguntas.q: Is it suitable to play with children?
preguntas.a: Yes, although the pet cockroach is always a bit creepy: it's part of the fun.

dinosaurios.descripcion: T-Rex alpha, complete fossil, Triceratops and perfect DNA in front of the approaching meteorite and the electric fence without light. The Jurassic Park theme brought to the game, with items that sound like an adventure movie.

preguntas.q: Is the meteorite really a bad item?
preguntas.a: Yes, and very feared: it is the reminder that it was fatal for the dinosaurs.

granja.descripcion: John Deere tractor, dairy cow, laying hen and forest cabin with aphid infestation and manure. The most rural theme in the catalog: perfect to play with a family who spends their summers in the town.

preguntas.q: Is the John Deere tractor as good as they say?
preguntas.a: Yes, it is the most sought-after item in the theme: without a tractor there is no functioning farm.

atraco.descripcion: Brain of the operation, hacker, professional driver and weapons expert in front of the digging spoon and forgotten gloves. The theme of perfect robberies: here the important thing is not the loot, but not staying with the weak link in the gang, and there are items that condemn the entire operation.

preguntas.q: What is the worst item of the robbery?
preguntas.a: The digging spoon: in a robbery gang it is absolutely useless, and at the auction it is the most remembered punishment.

detective.descripcion: Sherlock Holmes, Hercule Poirot, Columbo and Adrian Monk investigate an auction with a broken magnifying glass and a mute witness. The theme for those who watch police series and have already guessed everything before the end.

preguntas.q: Who is Adrian Monk?
preguntas.a: The obsessive-compulsive detective of the Monk series; it is one of the most beloved items in the theme.

acampada.descripcion: Tent, campfire, lake and smores against the flooded tent, mosquitoes and mud. The theme of sleeping away from home: everything that is good about camping and everything that goes wrong.

preguntas.q: What can't be missing when camping?
preguntas.a: The tent and the bonfire: without them there is no worthwhile camping, neither in the game nor outside.

futbol_historicos.descripcion: Di Stéfano, Cruyff, Beckenbauer and Garrincha against Cubillas, the little-known Peruvian who closes the list. The theme of the retired: Messi and Cristiano do not come into play here, as they already have their own theme in Soccer.

preguntas.q: Why aren't Messi or Cristiano there?
preguntas.a: Because they are still active in recent memory and have their place in Soccer; here only retired legends.

true_crime.descripcion: Alcàsser, Zodiac, Black Dahlia and Jack the Ripper against the psychic, the tabloid and the bar rumor. The theme of the real cases: only history and legend, no recent victims.

preguntas.q: Are they all real cases?
preguntas.a: Yes, historical or legendary; the theme expressly avoids recent or sensitive cases.

draft-de-20-monedas.titulo: What is the 20 coin draft: the TikTok trend that is played with two mobile phones
draft-de-20-monedas.desc: The 20-coin draft came from TikTok: fixed budget, item list, and turn-based bidding. This is the trend and this is how you play for free in Draft 20.
draft-de-20-monedas.h1: What is the 20 coin draft (the TikTok trend)

p: The 20 coin draft is a format that became popular on TikTok and Reels with videos like "You have $20": a list of characters, objects or dishes appears, each with a price, and you have to assemble the best possible team without going over the budget. The trick is not in knowing more than anyone else, but in choosing well with the right money.

Over time the format evolved from “choose from a list” to “bid on each item”, and that's where it gets really fun: it's no longer enough to have a budget, you have to fight for each item against another person.

Draft 20 turns that trend into a two-player duel: 8 rounds, 20 coins each and a theme per game (soccer, anime, food, streamers...). In each round an item goes up for auction and players bid in turns with BID +1 or BID +3. When someone drops out, the last bidder pays the price and takes the item.

The value of each item is secret until the end: during the game you only see its emoji and its name, so the winner is the one who best interprets what the opponent wants and not the one who knows the list by heart. When finished, whoever has collected the most ⭐ wins; if there is a tie, it is decided by remaining coins.

There are two details that change the game: each player can take a maximum of 4 items (the following are passed to the rival) and, if you run out of coins, you give up the item and the rival decides whether to keep it for 1 🪙 or give it to you.

A game lasts about five minutes, you don't have to register, you don't have to download anything and you play from your mobile browser. Each player uses their own phone: one creates the room, shares a 5-character code via WhatsApp and the rival enters from wherever they are.

That makes it the ideal game for video calls, to kill some dead time or for daily play with the same person. And if you don't have a rival on hand, you can always practice against the bot in four difficulty levels.

The official version is 8 rounds and 20 coins, but the format supports variants without breaking. The most common is to change the budget: with 10 coins the game becomes an exercise in austerity in which every bid hurts, and with 30 coins the good items skyrocket in price and you have to know when to quit.

Another variant is the surprise theme: no one knows what the list is about until the first item comes out. In Draft 20 it is enough to choose "All (random)" when creating the room, although the strict way would be not to look at the name of the theme in the header during the first bid.

You can also play best of three: three games in a row with different themes and whoever wins two wins the series. It is the fairest way to measure who plays better, because a single theme can greatly favor a player.

como-ganar-draft-20.titulo: How to Win at Draft 20: 7 Bidding Tactics (and 3 Typical Mistakes)
como-ganar-draft-20.desc: Seven tactics to win in Draft 20: when to drop out, how to read your opponent and why not spend the 20 coins in the first round.
como-ganar-draft-20.h1: How to Win at Draft 20: Auction Tactics

secciones.h: Before you start: understand the game
p: In Draft 20, whoever adds the most ⭐ wins, not whoever spends the most coins. The value of each item is secret during the game and is only revealed at the end, so your budget serves two purposes: getting good items and denying good items to your opponent. Almost all tactics are born from that tension.
Each game has 8 rounds and a maximum of 4 items per player. If you reach the cap, the items that come out later go directly to the rival, so the cap is also managed.

secciones.h: Tactic 1: Don't spend everything in the first round
p: The item you love may come out in round 1 and a similar one in round 5 for half the price. If you bid to the end in the first auction, you are left with less than 15 coins for seven rounds. Rule of thumb: in the first two rounds, set a ceiling (for example, don't go over 6) and stick to it.

secciones.h: Tactic 2: Learn to Drop Out (I'M OUT)
p: The most profitable button in the game is I'M OUT when your rival is the last to bid: they pay the price and take the item, but you avoid paying more and force them to spend. Dropping out is not losing: it is making your rival finance the auction.

In a few rounds you can see the personality of each player: the one who bids +3 in the first bid is usually in a hurry, the one who bids +1 is always watching their coins. If you detect that someone never drops out, let another item that you don't need climb high.

secciones.h: Tactic 4: Save for the Last Round
p: In the last rounds there is usually less competition because your rivals are already near the cap or short on coins. Arriving at round 7 with 10-12 coins is a brutal advantage: you can take two items in a row at a bargain price.

Winning is not about collecting everything shiny: it is about adding more than your rival. A player with four well-chosen average items usually beats one with two star items and two bad ones, because the average matters. Don't dismiss a solid item if it's cheap.

If you reach 4 items, everything that comes out after goes to the rival. Use it to your advantage: when you have three items, bid on the next one and leave the leftovers so your rival can't choose. And if your rival already has 3 items, the next one that comes out already has an owner.

secciones.h: Tactic 7: Change the Theme in the Rematch
p: If you lose a game, a rematch with the same theme benefits the one who already knows the list. Changing the theme (or leaving “All (random)”) balances the next one. It is the cheapest way to keep the competition even.

1) Always bid +3 out of impatience: spending money too quickly. 2) Drop out whenever the price goes up: the rival gets all the good items at a low price. 3) Forget the cap: when the rival already has 4 items, continuing to bid high is giving them coins for nothing.

faq.q: Can you win without ever bidding?
faq.a: No, but you can win by bidding little: if you lower yourself judiciously and let your rival spend, there comes a time when he can no longer bid and you take the last items.

faq.q: How is a tie decided?
faq.a: If you both end up with the same ⭐, whoever keeps the most coins wins. If there is also a tie, it is a draw.

juegos-de-subasta-online.titulo: Online auction games: how to choose the best one to play with friends
juegos-de-subasta-online.desc: Comparison of free online auction games: what to look for, which ones work best for two players and how to start playing without installing anything.
juegos-de-subasta-online.h1: Online auction games to play with friends

secciones.h: What makes a good auction game
p: An auction game works when decisions are irreversible and information is imperfect: if you know exactly what everything is worth and can rectify it, the tension disappears. The best ones add two things: short games (so you can play several in a row) and a human rival.

Online there are three families: auctions within board games (Tarot, Bids, Modern Art), auction simulators for one player (those for storage rooms and pawn shops) and auction duels for two people like Draft 20.

It is a turn-based auction duel for two players: 8 rounds, 20 coins and one theme per game among 69 available. Each player uses their own mobile phone and enters with a 5-character code, without registration or download.

What makes it different is the secret value: you don't see the ⭐ of each item until the end, so the auction is about reading the rival, not calculating. If you want to try it, you can create a room or practice against the bot.

If you like "table" auctions, in Board Game Arena there are classics such as French Tarot or Bids, with complete rules and rivals from all over the world. The downside: they are longer games (20-24 minutes) and you need to know the rules before starting.

Storage room and pawn shop games, like Bid Wars, are fun for free time, but they play against the machine: there is no real bidding or reading of the rival. They are good if you are looking for progression, not competition.

Do you want to play with another person from your own phone and in less than 10 minutes? You need a web duel like Draft 20. Looking for a deep board game with more players? Board Game Arena. Do you play alone and want to progress? An auction simulator.

secciones.h: How to set up an auction night
p: If you want to turn the auctions into an evening plan, the most practical thing is to alternate games: start with a couple of Draft 20 games (five minutes each, with a change of theme in between) and end with a longer auction board game if the group can handle it.

The key is in the variety of themes: a general culture theme for those who know everything, another about food for those who don't, and a random one to break the tie. Thus, no one always wins by knowing more, and the competitive spirit continues throughout the night.

faq.q: What is the best auction game for two people?
faq.a: If you're looking for quick, mobile games, Draft 20 is designed exactly for two players with hidden information. For long sessions, the Board Game Arena classics.

faq.q: Are there free auction games?
faq.a: Yes: Draft 20 is free and ad-free, and Board Game Arena has a free plan with a full catalog.

secciones.h: What does a game need to work on WhatsApp

That's why games that meet three conditions work best: they are entered with a link or a short code, they are played in turns (no one has to be looking at the screen at the same time) and they don't require you to install an app.
Short duration is another advantage: if a game does not exceed 10 minutes, it is much easier to repeat without getting bored.

You create the room and WhatsApp gives you a 5-character code to share; the other enters from his mobile with that code. The two bid in turns until completing 8 rounds and whoever collects the most ⭐ wins. When finished, the game itself offers a button to propose a rematch and a new code is generated.
It is the fastest on the list and the only one designed exclusively for two players, without groups or shared screens.

The web version of the pen and paper classic. Everyone writes at the same time in categories ("name, thing, city...") and the timer scores alone. Ideal for WhatsApp groups, although you need everyone to be connected at the same time.

The drawing version of broken telephone: each player writes a sentence, the next one draws it, the next one describes the drawing and at the end the chain is revealed. With 6 or more people it is a laughter machine; with only two it falls flat.
Two teams try to guess words with single-word clues. You need at least four people and some patience with the rules, but it's the best word game for groups that already know each other.

The classic icebreaker: you can play directly in the chat, writing the questions and challenges, without any website in between. It works better in groups and in moments of boredom than in serious games.

secciones.h: How to set up a game in 3 steps
p: 1) Open the game and create a room from your phone. 2) Share the code or link via WhatsApp (many games, including Draft 20, have a button to send it directly). 3) When the other enters, the game starts automatically.

secciones.h: Typical errors when organizing games on WhatsApp
p: The first is not to agree on the time: in turn-based games it is necessary for both to be available, so it is advisable to notify before creating the room. The second is to send the code without context when the other person is at work; the link works the same, but no one enters blindly.

The third is to play with a bad connection: if the opponent takes more than 45 seconds without responding, the game is considered abandoned. On an unstable mobile network it is better to wait until you have coverage before starting.

faq.q: Can you play Draft 20 from a WhatsApp group?
faq.a: Draft 20 is for two players: the link or code is shared through the group chat, but the game is played between two people.

faq.q: Do we need to be connected at the same time?
faq.a: Yes, in turn-based games like Draft 20 the game advances when both respond. If someone is absent, the game notifies you after 6 seconds and the room closes after 45 seconds without activity.

draft-20-vs-you-have-20.titulo: Draft 20 vs You Have $20: differences and which one to choose
draft-20-vs-you-have-20.desc: We compare Draft 20 and You Have $20 (trend app): platform, price, number of players, themes and languages, so you can choose according to your case.

secciones.h: Two ways to play the same trend
p: The “you have $20” format went viral on TikTok with lists of characters and a fixed budget. Very different proposals have come from there: You Have $20 took it to an iPhone app designed to play several games around a single phone, and Draft 20 turned it into an online duel between two players, each with their own mobile phone.
It's not that one is better: they solve different situations. This comparison is informative and neither is affiliated with the other.
Platform: You Have $20 is an iOS app (App Store); Draft 20 is played in the browser, on Android, iPhone or PC.

Price: in You Have $20 the games with random category are free and the extra options (choose category or create them with AI) come with PRO subscription; Draft 20 is free, with all themes available and without advertising.
Players: in You Have $20, two people bid on the same phone and the rest act as judges; in Draft 20 exactly two players play, each on their device, with a room code.
Content: You Have $20 offers about 40 categories in 25 languages; Draft 20 has 69 themes with 20 items each, with a very Spanish accent (tapas, soccer, streamers).
Registration: neither of us ask for it.

secciones.h: Which one to choose according to your case
p: If you are on an iPhone and four people want to play at the same time with a single cell phone on the table, an app like You Have $20 fits better.

If there are two of you and you are not in the same place (or yes, but you want each one with your own screen), Draft 20 is more direct: room with code, five-minute games, one-touch rematch and zero installation.
If your group is on Android or mixes devices, the browser wins by a landslide: Draft 20 works on any phone without downloading anything.

Both respect the essence of the trend: fixed budget, items with hidden values until the end and a decision that is regretted or celebrated for days. And in both, the subsequent discussion ("I had a better collection") is part of the game.

secciones.h: What we would like to see in both
p: Both projects still have a way to go: the native apps need to be played on their own device without complications, and the browser games need to reach more languages and have a larger community for tournaments.
The important thing is that the 20-coin draft trend is no longer just a TikTok video: it can now be played for real, with clear rules and immediate rematches, in either format.

faq.q: Are Draft 20 and You Have $20 the same thing?
faq.a: No. They share the format of the 20-coin draft trend, but they are independent projects: one is an iOS app for group play, and the other is a two-player online browser game.

faq.q: Does Draft 20 work on Android?
faq.a: Yes, and also on iPhone and PC: you play from the browser, without installing any app.

faq.q: Is there a free version of You Have $20?
faq.a: Yes, games with surprise category are free; the options to choose or create categories are part of your PRO subscription.

p: At a family meal there are two classic problems: not everyone knows how to play the same thing and no one wants to explain rules for half an hour. secciones.h: How to set up the game in 3 steps

secciones.h: What to do if there are many of you at the table

faq.q: Can you play with children at Christmas?

juegos-verano.titulo: Games for summer: themes to play in the sun

secciones.h: The Perfect Game for Summer Downtime
p: In summer there is plenty of time and no plan: the nap, the wait at the beach bar, the return from the campsite. Draft 20 fits because a game lasts five minutes and is played on two mobile phones, each with its own screen, even if you have not met before.
You don't have to install anything or register and, if the beach's Wi-Fi fails, the game continues from your mobile phone with data.

For the beach bar plan, nothing like Tapas and Bar with a cold Craft Beer: Iberian ham, tortilla and Galician-style octopus against the last olive on the plate. And if there are embers involved, the Sunday BBQ extends the meal with steak against wet charcoal.

secciones.h: Challenges to play in a group
p: The best way to play in a group is a quick league: two play and the winner stays for the next duel. In half an hour four or five people pass through the auction and the excitement builds on its own.
Another option is a theme per game, with random activated: this way no one can prepare a strategy and all the duels are different.

The value of each item is secret until the end, so in summer the auction is about reading the rival and not knowing the list. If you play with "Visible Values" activated, you will be able to see the ⭐ of each item and decide more calmly, although the game loses some of its mystery.

For games in the sun, quick mode works best: short themes (Tapas, Pizza, Craft Beer), few coins and instant rematch. And if someone runs out of battery, the game runs just as well on a tablet or laptop in the shade.

secciones.h: What to bring (and what not to) to play on the beach
p: You don't need anything more than a cell phone per player and some coverage. It is better not to play with your phone in direct sunlight (it gets hot and the screen looks bad) and avoid the edge of salt water. With two towels, an umbrella and ten minutes you have a complete game.
If you are going to play several in a row, take turns: those who wait act as judges and are in charge of keeping things going, which is half the fun of the draft.

faq.q: Can you play offline on the beach?

secciones.h: Three ways to play as a couple

And if you have any energy left, the rematch with a random theme is the best ending: no one gets to pick their preferred theme and the series is truly decided. The series score is saved on your phone, so you can continue it another day.

juegos-por-videollamada.titulo: Games to play via video call with a friend (Discord, Zoom or FaceTime)
juegos-por-videollamada.desc: Which games really work on a video call, what to look for and why Draft 20 fits: without installing anything, with link or code and 5-minute games.
juegos-por-videollamada.h1: Games to play over video call with a friend

secciones.h: What really works in a video call
p: Playing via video call has an unwritten rule: if the game forces you to look at another screen for more than a few seconds, the conversation dies, and so does the game. That's why games with clear turns work best, rules that are explained in a sentence, and short games that can be commented on while playing.

The second factor is technical friction. Asking someone to sign up, install an app, or create an account kills the game before it begins. The ideal is a game that you enter with a link, without downloads, and that works the same from your mobile or computer.

And the third is the competitive spark. A video-call game only works if there are decisions, tension and something to tell at the end. Bluffing or bidding turns do this much better than pure luck games.

secciones.h: Why auction games are such a good fit
p: The auction adds just what a call is missing: shared decision moments. In each round there is a very brief pause in which one bids, the other hesitates and in the video call the "really?" is heard. That two-second tension is all the entertainment.

Furthermore, the auction explains itself: there are items, each one is worth something secret, and whoever puts together the best collection wins. You can explain it in twenty seconds and you can start playing with the other person without them having read a single rule.

secciones.h: How to play Draft 20 via video call
p: Open Draft 20 on your mobile and share the room link through the call chat (WhatsApp, Discord, Telegram or the Zoom chat itself). Your friend enters with his name and you are already playing: 8 rounds, 20 coins each and a surprise theme.

Since it is not necessary to talk about the game to play it, the call is filled with other things: commenting on the items, laughing at the ones that no one wants and showing off the final collection. When you finish you can press QUICK REMATCH and continue with another theme without sharing anything again.
If you prefer to play without a call, the code works the same; and if you want to practice before, there is a practice mode against the bot with adjustable difficulty.

secciones.h: Errors that ruin a video call game
p: The first is to choose a game with long turns: if each player thinks for thirty seconds, the call becomes two people looking at the cell phone in silence. Draft 20 turns are resolved in seconds and that keeps the conversation alive.

The second is not agreeing when to finish. A short game is enjoyable; five in a row without pause end in fatigue. The usual thing is to play two or three, comment on the last one and decide whether there's a rematch.

The third is to play with someone who is doing something else: in an auction, half the fun is reacting to what the other person is doing. If the opponent responds after two minutes, the tension disappears.

faq.q: Do I need to install something to play via video call?
faq.a: No. Draft 20 is played in the browser: share a link or code and that's it. The video call goes through your usual application (Discord, Zoom, FaceTime, Meet).

faq.q: Can you play from your mobile with mobile data?
faq.a: Yes, the game is lightweight and only sends small requests every second. With a normal mobile connection it is enough.

faq.q: How long does a game last?
faq.a: Between 4 and 8 minutes. There are 8 rounds and each round is a few seconds of bidding, so allow time for several games in one call.

faq.q: Does it work for more than two players?
faq.a: No: Draft 20 is a two-player duel. If there are more of you, it is played in pairs and each couple shares the screen or takes turns.

juegos-online-gratis-sin-registro.titulo: Free online games without downloading or registration for 2 players
juegos-online-gratis-sin-registro.desc: How to recognize free online games that really require no registration, no downloads, no invasive ads, and options to play with a friend instantly.

p: Most websites that say “no registration” ask for an email on the second click, or force you to install an application. A truly registration-free game gives you a room and a link (or a short code): whoever opens it can jump straight in with a name, and that's it.
That detail changes the entire experience. There is no waiting, no password to remember and no profile to fill out: play now and, if you like it, come back another day.

secciones.h: What to look at before choosing a free game
p: First, friction: how many clicks are there between landing on the site and your first move? If there are more than two, bad. Second, the ads: banners that jump or block the buttons make it impossible to play on mobile. Third, privacy: a serious game does not need your personal data to let you play a game.
And finally, clarity: rules that are explained in one sentence and short games. If you need a ten-minute tutorial before your first game, that's a game for another time.

secciones.h: Draft 20: free, in the browser and without accounts
p: Draft 20 is a two-player bidding duel that works exactly like this: you enter, choose a theme (or let it be random), share the link and play 8 rounds of bidding. There is no account or download required, and there are currently no ads.

No data is required to play either: the session lives in your browser and local progress (record, achievements and series) is saved on your own device. It is free in the browser and, if you prefer, it can be installed as an application from your mobile phone with one button, without going through a store.
And if no one is available to play at that time, there is a quick game against another person or practice against the bot with four difficulties.

secciones.h: How to Spot a "Free" Game with a Catch
p: Real free games are sustained without asking you anything before playing. The warning signs are clear: a registration form before the first game, a limit of attempts that is unlocked by paying, or virtual coins that are purchased to continue playing.

It's also a good idea to look at the ads: a banner on the side is acceptable, but those that cover buttons or open new tabs turn the game into an aiming exercise. And if the game promises real prizes for playing, be suspicious: the product is most likely you.

faq.q: Does Draft 20 ask for email or account?

faq.q: Do you have ads or microtransactions?
faq.a: Currently there are no ads, no purchases, and no microtransactions: the 20 coins and 8 rounds are the same for everyone.

faq.q: Do I need to create a room or can I play now?
faq.a: You can press Quick play and the system will match you with the first player looking for a game; or create a room and share the code.

secciones.h: The problem of playing two with nothing at hand
p: When there are only two of you and there are no board games, cards or consoles nearby, the options are quickly reduced: either you use your cell phone or you improvise. The good news is that with one cell phone per person you already have a plan, because the best games for two do not need material, just the desire to play games.
The key is that the game works with what you already have and that it is explained in a minute. If you have to read rules for ten minutes, the plan dies before it starts.

Draft 20 is designed just for this: two players, two mobile phones and five minutes. Each one has 20 coins, one item comes out per round and you bid in turns; whoever collects the most valuable collection wins. Without registration, without downloads and with 69 themes to never repeat.

To begin with, Pizza and Soccer are infallible because everyone knows the items. If you already like to play, Board Games turns the game into a geek duel: Colonists against Viruses in the same auction.

secciones.h: Classics that never fail without material
p: The 20 questions game works with any topic: one thinks something and the other has 20 yes/no to guess it. With couples or friends who know each other a lot, it's surprisingly fun and requires nothing.

The best of 7 rock, paper, scissors with tests for the loser (choose the next topic, invite to the round) also saves any wait. And if you are in a bar, playing to guess the next song they will play is a classic that never gets old.

secciones.h: If you are each at home: video call
p: At a distance, the video call plus a turn-based game is the winning combination: everyone looks at their screen and speaks through the hands-free device. Draft 20 works like this without adaptation, because the turns are already in order and it is not necessary to see the screens.
Set it up like this: one creates the room, shares the 5-letter code on WhatsApp and the other enters. The first game will serve to learn; from the second the real kick begins.

secciones.h: How not to always repeat the same thing
p: The trick so that the plan for two does not run out is to rotate: one game with a known theme (Pizza), another with a random one ("All") and another with something that neither of them controls, such as Music or Soccer for those who are not soccer fans. Random is the one that makes the most laughs, because no one can prepare a strategy.
And when one wins two in a row, a rematch with another theme is mandatory: it is the unwritten rule that keeps any duel alive.

faq.q: What games can you play together without buying anything?
faq.a: In-browser Draft 20, 20 Questions, Rock-Paper-Scissors with Quizzes, and Song Guessing Games – none of which require materials or downloads.

faq.q: Can you play two each from your home?
faq.a: Yes: with a video call and a turn-based game like Draft 20, which is played on two mobile phones with a room code shared by WhatsApp.

faq.q: How long does a Draft 20 game last?
faq.a: About five minutes: 8 rounds of turn-based bidding with 20 coins per player. Perfect for chaining rematches.

p: There are gaps in the day that don't allow for a board game but seem eternal: the wait for the bus, the coffee break, the doctor's waiting room, the announcements before the movie. A five-minute game turns those moments into healthy play instead of infinite scrolling.
The ideal format is always the same: one-minute rules, five-minute game and immediate rematch if someone is left wanting.

A game of Draft 20 lasts about five minutes: 8 turn-based auction rounds, 20 coins per player and one theme per game. It is played in the mobile browser, without registration, so the time from "shall we play?" Even the first bid is seconds.
For quick games, the best themes are the ones that are easy to recognize: Burger, Tapas or Pizza. Everyone knows what an omelet or a mushroom is, and the decisions come by themselves.

secciones.h: More short games for two without material
p: The "I spy" with categories (only car brands, only foods) lasts surprisingly well for five minutes between two. Another option is the turn-based alphabet game with a category: A for olive, B for cod... whoever gets stuck loses.
And the classic of counting to 20 by taking turns saying one or two numbers (whoever says 20 wins) seems silly until you try not to lose twice in a row.

secciones.h: Tricks so that the game does not drag on
p: In Draft 20, if you want it to be a real five minutes, play with a known theme and without stopping to calculate each bid: the first games are decided by instinct and are just as fun. The tactic comes alone from the third.
Choose who starts alternating (the one who lost the previous one starts the next one) and have a rematch in one tap: the rhythm of game-after-game is what hooks you, not a single perfect game.

secciones.h: When to chain and when to stop
p: Three games in a row are the sweet spot: about fifteen minutes that fly by and leave the score (2-1) for the next time. More than five in a row and the competition turns into stubbornness.
Always leave a rematch pending for another day: "I'll beat you in Music tomorrow" is the best way for a quick game to become a tradition.

estrategia.titulo: How to play Draft 20 and win: rules and complete strategy
estrategia.desc: Complete guide to Draft 20: concept, rules of the 8 rounds, management of the 20 coins, bidding psychology (bluffing, inflating prices, forcing cost overruns) and strategies by theme.
estrategia.h1: How to play Draft 20 and win: complete strategy
intro: Draft 20 is an auction duel for two players: 8 rounds, 20 coins per player and one theme per game. Each round an item goes up for auction, you bid in turns and whoever takes it adds it to their team of 4. The winner is whoever adds the most stars at the end. The rules are learned in two minutes; winning consistently requires managing your coins, reading the opponent and knowing the theme.

This guide is the complete manual: first the step-by-step rules and then the strategy that separates those who improvise from those who win series. If you just want the rules, they are summarized on the how to play page.

p: The idea comes from the viral videos of the "20 dollar draft": a fixed budget to be distributed among a list of items, where the fun is in choosing well and not in being able to pay more than anyone else. Draft 20 turns that dynamic into a duel with real rules: the budget is 20 coins, the list is 20 items of a theme and the distribution is decided by bidding, not voting.

Each game pits two players against each other with the same conditions: the same 20 coins, the same 8 drawn items from the theme and the same information. There is no chance after the initial draw or hidden advantages: if you lose, it is because your rival bid better than you. And with a rematch just a tap away, there is always a second chance with another theme.

A game has exactly 8 rounds and each round auctions off a different item. Each player's final collection has a maximum of 4 items: when someone reaches 4, the items that come out later are automatically passed to the opponent. That way, the 8 rounds always split 4-4.

ul: Round 1 to 8: an item from the theme comes out with its initial price at 0.
The player whose turn it is starts: he can BID +1, BID +3 or fold with I'M OUT.
The turns alternate until one of the two drops out: the last player to bid pays the final price and takes the item.
If it is your turn to bid and you do not have coins, press PASS and the rival decides: keep the item for 1 coin or give it to you.
The star value of each item (from 1 to 10) is secret until the end, unless you play with visible values.
Upon completing the 8 rounds, whoever adds the most stars wins; if there is a tie, whoever keeps the most coins wins.

p: The starting order matters: whoever starts the round places the first bid and sets the tone, but whoever drops out last decides who pays. That's why the game is not about winning bids, but about paying a fair price for the items you want and a high price for those your rival wants.

You have 20 coins for 4 items: the fair average is 5 coins per item. Every extra coin you pay for one item is money taken away from the other three, and everything you save on a mediocre item you can invest in the star of the list. Bankroll management isn't about gut feelings, but about two simple rules.

Reserve about 6-7 coins (one third) for the second half of the game. The big items usually come out when you have already spent, and reaching rounds 6-8 without coins turns you into a spectator: the rival takes the best at whatever price they want. If mid-game you have spent more than 13-14 coins, you are paying too much.

bloques.h3: When to spend and when to save

p: Spend heavily only on game-changing items: those that are clearly worth 8 or more stars in their theme. In the rest, your objective is not to get them cheap, but to force your rival to pay dearly for them (see psychology). And never stay at zero on purpose: without coins you lose the bidding turn and the rival decides for you with the PASS rule.

ul: Average budget per item: 5 coins; more than 7 on a normal item means overpaying.
By mid-game (round 4) you should have at least 6-7 coins.
The tie is broken by remaining coins: each coin saved is worth double.

bloques.h2: Bidding psychology: bluffing, inflating and forcing

p: Since the values are secret, the auction is an information game: each bid says something about what you think the item is worth, and so does every fold. Whoever lies best and reads best, wins. These are the three weapons.

bloques.h3: The bluff: bidding what you don't want

p: Bidding hard for a mediocre item makes your rival believe that it is a gem, and sometimes they end up paying more for fear of leaving it to you cheap. Bluffing works best at the beginning of the game, when everyone's tastes are not yet known, and in moderation: if you are discovered, your opponent will stop believing you when you really bid.

bloques.h3: Inflating prices: the rise that doesn't hurt

p: When your opponent clearly wants an item, every +1 or +3 you add before dropping is money they won't have later. The technique is to go up one at a time until you notice them hesitate, and drop out just before the price commits you. An item they would have paid 4 for and end up taking at 7 is 3 coins less for the rest of the game.

bloques.h3: Force extra costs on the rival

p: The advanced version of inflating: identify the item that the opponent absolutely needs (for example, the last gap on their team) and squeeze it to the limit. If they need that item to complete 4, they'll pay almost anything and come out of that round with no coins for whatever comes next. Of course: calculate well, because if they drop out before you, you pay the extra cost.

Not all themes play the same, because not all lists are built the same. In the themes you master (Pizza, Soccer), trust your judgment: you know which items are elite and which are filler. In those that you do not dominate, manage your coins and read your opponent: spend little, inflate a lot and save for the end.

ul: Known themes (Pizza, Soccer): identify your 2-3 elite items before you start and go for them; the rest is currency to inflate.
Culture themes (Board games, Music): if the rival knows more than you, do not compete in knowledge; compete on bankroll management and let him pay dearly for his wisdom.
Random theme ("All"): no one can prepare anything, so whoever improvises best wins: cheap bluffs, coins for the end and zero attachment to any item.
With the cap of 4 in mind: if you already have 3 items and there is little left, each coin is worth more, because the opponent knows that you need to close the team.
Without coins (PASS): if the rival gives you the item, sometimes it is because it is worth little; if you keep it for 1, it was better than it seemed. Write down that information.

p: And the last strategy isn't for a single game, but for the whole series: always play the rematch with another theme. Changing lists resets the opponent's reads and rewards the most well-rounded player, not the most specialized one.

faq.desc: We resolve doubts about Draft 20: private rooms and invitations, how it is scored, what happens if you disconnect, available themes and how to play on mobile.
intro: Here are the answers to what we get asked the most: how to set up a game with a friend, how the winner is decided, what happens if the connection drops mid-round and what devices you can play on.

faq.q: How do I create a private room to play with a friend?
faq.a: From the main page, write your name, choose the theme (or leave "All" to be drawn) and press create room. You will get a 5-letter code that you can share on WhatsApp or with the direct invitation link: your rival opens it, enters with his name and the game starts automatically, without registration.

faq.q: How is the score calculated and who wins?
faq.a: Each item has a secret value from 1 to 10 stars that is only revealed at the end. Whoever adds the most stars with their 4 items wins. If there is a star tie, whoever has saved the most coins wins, so every coin you save counts double.

faq.q: What happens if I log out mid-round?
faq.a: You can log in again with the same room code from the same browser and you will recover your site, because the session is saved on your device. If you abandon permanently, the game does not count towards the statistics and your opponent can continue practicing or ask for a rematch at another time.

faq.q: How many themes are there and which are the best to start with?
faq.a: There are 69 themes of 20 items each, with a selection of Featured that rotates with trends. To start we recommend Pizza and Soccer, because everyone recognizes the items; when you control the game, the "All" option determines the theme in each game and none of them are repeated.

faq.q: Can it be played on mobile? Do I need to install something?
faq.a: Yes, and you don't have to install anything: it is played in the mobile browser, with large buttons designed for touch screens. If you want, you can add it to the home screen as another app; it will work in full screen and with its own icon.

faq.q: Can I play alone against the machine?
faq.a: Yes, with the practice mode: you choose the theme and difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard or Extreme) and the bot takes the second seat with the same rules as you. You also have guided practice, which explains each step while you play on easy. And from the tab for each theme you can directly enter a game against the bot in one click.

faq.q: How does the rematch work?
faq.a: At the end of the game, either of the two can propose a rematch with a new theme from the final screen. The opponent accepts or rejects it right there, and whoever starts the first round alternates so that no one has an advantage. The chained rematches form a best-of-3 series.

faq.q: Do I need to register or pay anything?
faq.a: No: it's free and without accounts. You enter with a temporary name, play and that's it. There are no payments, no subscriptions, no real coins: the 20 coins are just the budget for each game.

faq.q: What are visible values (⭐)?
faq.a: It is an optional mode that shows the stars of each item during the game, instead of keeping them secret until the end. It is chosen by whoever creates the room and affects both players. It is ideal for learning, although the game loses part of the mystery and bluffing.

faq.q: How long does a game last?
faq.a: About five minutes: 8 rounds of turn-based bidding with quick decisions. It is perfect for chaining two or three in a row during a break, and the rematch is set up in seconds with another theme.

faq.q: Can more than two people play?
faq.a: The games are 1 on 1 duels, but with more people the normal thing is to set up a league: two play, the winner stays and the next challenger enters. The rest can act as a jury and vote for the best team at the end, as in the original trend videos.

faq.q: Are my games and statistics saved?
faq.a: Your results are saved in your own browser (wins, streaks and achievements), without accounts or servers with your data. Only anonymous statistics of finished games (theme and mode) are recorded for the monthly ranking of the most played, without names or identifiers.

hub.desc: What is an auction game, why it is so engaging and how to choose one online for two players: mechanics, variants and Draft 20 explained.
hub.h1: Auction games: what they are and why they are engaging
hub.intro: An auction game turns a simple decision (“how much do I pay for this?”) into an entire system: there are items, there is a price that goes up, and there is someone on the other side who wants the same thing as you. Here's what makes a good auction game, what variants exist, and where to play one online for free with someone else.

p: In an auction game, players compete to take objects (items, cards, characters, plates of food) by bidding on them. Normally each player starts with the same budget, and the game consists of deciding how much it is worth paying for each thing that comes out: if you pay more, you run out of money for the good stuff; if you pay less, someone else takes it.

The funny thing is that the value of what you buy is not always public. In some games you see a score; in others, like Draft 20, the value of each item is secret until the end, so the person who best interprets what the opponent wants wins, not the person who knows the list by heart.

secciones.h: Variants: sealed envelope, open bid and round-robin auction
p: The sealed-bid auction is the classic one: each player writes his bid at the same time and the highest one wins the lot. She is quick, but has little conversation: there is no tension during the bidding, only when opening the envelopes.

Open bidding (auction house style) is more lively: the price rises and anyone can outbid until everyone else withdraws. It generates much more tension, although it usually requires an agile rhythm so as not to drag on forever.

The turn-based auction mixes the best of both: the price rises one at a time, each player decides at the time whether to go up or down, and whoever leaves lets the other pay. It's the mechanic of Draft 20, and it's the one that produces the funniest moments: that "I'll leave it to you" when your opponent thinks you've understood something you haven't.

secciones.h: What makes a good auction game
p: First, limited budget: if you can buy everything, there is no game. The limit is what forces you to choose. Second, imperfect information: if everyone knows the exact value of each item, the game is reduced to accounts; with hidden or partially hidden values, reading the opponent comes into play.

Third, short games with easy rematches. The auction leaves a clear flavor ("I was wrong in round 2") and that immediately calls for another game. And fourth, that you can play with someone without explaining half an hour of rules: the less preparation, the more people will sit at the table.

secciones.h: Draft 20: turn-based auction, online and free
p: Draft 20 takes this mechanic to a two-player duel in the browser: 20 coins each, 8 rounds and one theme per game (soccer, food, anime, streamers and 68 more). In each round an item goes up for auction and is bid in turns with BID +1 or BID +3; whoever drops out lets the last bidder pay the price and keep the item.

There are two rules that give it character: each player can hoard a maximum of 4 items (from then on, the items go to the rival) and, if you run out of coins in a new round, you give up the item and the rival decides whether to keep it for 1 coin or give it to you. In the end, whoever adds the most ⭐ wins and, in the event of a tie, whoever keeps the most coins.
There is no account or download: create a room, share the code or link and play (currently ad-free). There is also quick play (automatic pairing) and practice against the bot in four difficulties.

secciones.h: How to get started in two minutes
p: Choose a theme from the catalog—or let it be random—and share the link with the other person. If you want to arrive with your homework done, start by understanding three concepts: what a bid is, what I'M OUT means and how the 4-item cap works. With that you already play your first game and, above all, you understand why the second is better than the first.

faq.q: What is the difference between an auction and a draft?
faq.a: In a draft you choose in turns from a common list and what one takes cannot be taken by another; in an auction you bid with a budget and you can pay more or less for the same thing. Draft 20 combines both: 8 items, 20 coins and turn-based bidding.

faq.q: What is the best auction game for two players?
faq.a: It depends on what you're looking for: if you want 5-minute games, without registration and from your mobile, Draft 20 is designed exactly for that. If you are looking for auctions with more components, there are classic board games of the genre, but they require material and presence.

faq.q: Can you play online auctions for free?
faq.a: Yes. Draft 20 is free, played in the browser and does not require an account. The 20 coins and 8 rounds are the same for everyone.

faq.q: Is the auction about skill or luck?
faq.a: In Draft 20 it is about skill: the items that come out are random, but the value is fixed and what you decide (when to bid, when to drop out, what collection to build) determines the result.
